title: Get one month ahead on your bills before you invest a cent
hooks: The month I stopped living paycheck to paycheck, I was actually a full month ahead on my bills.
Here is the budgeting trick that quietly ended my end-of-month panic.
You do not need more income to feel calm about money, you need a one-month buffer.
talking_points: List every fixed bill with a due date: HDB loan or rent, utilities, phone, insurance premiums, subscriptions, debt repayments.
For variable bills like electricity, use your highest recent month so you are never caught short.
Build that total plus a small buffer in a separate savings account before you spend from it.
Once funded, you pay this month from last month's money, so one bad week no longer breaks you.

title: Finance jargon, explained like a human: EBITDA
hooks: EBITDA sounds like a password, but it is just one honest question about a business.
Here is the finance term people nod along to and secretly do not understand.
If a company's earnings look amazing, this word tells you how much was makeup.
talking_points: EBITDA means earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation.
It strips out financing and accounting choices to compare the raw operating performance of businesses.
It is useful but can be dressed up, so never read it without looking at actual cash flow and debt.
The lesson for your own money: one flattering number never tells the whole story, in business or your budget.

title: Travel rewards without the debt trap, the Singapore version
hooks: Miles can fund your next holiday, but only if you avoid the one mistake that funds the bank instead.
